title: BANTAH JOKOWI CIPTAKAN KERUSAKAN: "JANGAN SOK SUCI, TANGGUNG MASALAH INI BERSAMA"

## Email Summary

## Overview
This video features an interview with Hasan Nasbi, the newly appointed Head of the Presidential Communication Office, discussing the final days of President Jokowi's administration and the transition to President-elect Prabowo. Nasbi addresses public criticism regarding Jokowi's final year and clarifies the role of his new office, emphasizing its function in supporting the incoming administration while also managing current issues. A significant portion of the discussion focuses on refuting claims of Jokowi being responsible for the nation's "damage" and highlights the smooth, supportive transition process being facilitated by the current president for the next one.

## Key Highlights
Hasan Nasbi, in his new role as Head of the Presidential Communication Office, addressed public scrutiny over President Jokowi's final year in office. He acknowledged that while some critics, including figures like Mahfud MD, hold Jokowi accountable for perceived damage, it's unfair to place sole responsibility on the last year of his tenure. Nasbi argued that those making such accusations were also part of Jokowi's administration for the preceding nine years and should share the responsibility, emphasizing that not all of Jokowi's agendas were achieved, but many were, particularly in infrastructure. He stressed the importance of fairness and looking at the administration holistically, rather than focusing on isolated criticisms.

The conversation delved into the transition between the Jokowi and Prabowo administrations, with Nasbi painting a picture of a cooperative and supportive handover. He highlighted that the Presidential Communication Office is being established to primarily serve the upcoming Prabowo administration, even though its current professional duties lie with President Jokowi. Nasbi described this as a benchmark for power transitions in Indonesia, with the outgoing president actively preparing the ground for the successor, including budget allocations for 2025 and facilitating Prabowo's priority programs. He dismissed rumors of friction between Jokowi and Prabowo, citing their public interactions as evidence of a positive relationship and emphasizing that any perceived differences are normal human variations, not significant conflicts.

Nasbi also touched upon the complexities surrounding the Constitutional Court's (MK) decisions, particularly regarding the age limit for presidential and vice-presidential candidates, referencing MK Decision No. 90/PUU-XXI/2023 which allowed Gibran Rakabuming Raka to run. He noted the hypocrisy of certain groups who initially sought to overturn this decision but later defended it when it suited their interests, advocating for consistency and fairness in how legal decisions are viewed and debated. He stressed that while public discourse and debate are healthy, labeling individuals or actions as inherently "bad" or "sinful" based on differing opinions or outcomes, especially when legal processes have been followed, is unproductive and unfair.

## Implications
The establishment of the Presidential Communication Office and its forward-looking mandate under Hasan Nasbi signifies a strategic effort to manage public perception and ensure a smooth, coordinated narrative during the presidential transition. The discussion highlights ongoing debates about accountability for government performance and the fairness of political processes, reflecting the complexities of Indonesian political discourse as the nation navigates leadership changes and policy continuity. The emphasis on a supportive transition process suggests a focus on institutional stability and a move towards establishing positive precedents for future power transfers.
